title: Stem Cells and Regenerative Medicine
text: Stem cells are undifferentiated cells capable of self-renewal and differentiation into specialized cell types. Embryonic stem cells (ESCs), derived from the inner cell mass of blastocysts, are pluripotent and can become any cell in the body. Adult stem cells, found in various tissues, are more limited in their differentiation potential. Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), first created by Shinya Yamanaka in 2006, are adult cells reprogrammed back to a pluripotent state. Stem cell research holds promise for treating degenerative diseases like Parkinson's and diabetes, and for regenerating damaged tissues. Ethical concerns about ESCs have spurred development of iPSC technologies as alternatives.
